summary: Yuanxing Guo worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche, and held posts as a researcher at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism and at Jinling Scriptural Press.

Yuanying Shi worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under Dagong Heshang, Zengxi, Miaolian, Yekai, Bazhi Toutuo, and Tongzhi. He served as abbot at Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, and held leadership roles in the Buddhist Association of China.

Yudru Tsomu specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, advisors Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, and teachers James E. Bosson, Wesley M. Jacobsen, and Kent Buys.

Yuen Ren Chao worked in linguistics and sinology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1910), Cornell University (~1910–1914), and Harvard University (~1915–1918), later holding posts at Cornell, Harvard, Tsinghua (~1925–1929), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia was a Buddhist studies scholar who founded Huayan University, where he also served as a teacher.
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University from around 1965 to 1974 and later served as its president from around 2011 to 2015.
Yui Chi Lau specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Yingguang Qu and founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society.

Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held an attested post at the University of Maryland, College Park in 2012.

Yuichi Kajiyama worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, SOAS, Vienna, and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, and held professorships at Kyoto University (~1956–1989), Bukkyo University (1988–1997), and Soka University (1997–2001).

Yuishin Ito is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. He served as associate professor at Bukkyo University (1961–1997) and held leadership posts at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College and Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Yujiro Motora worked in philosophy, having studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912) and the Tokyo University of Education.
Yujun Endo worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Taisho University, attested as associate professor in 1991 and professor emeritus in 2014.
Yuka Otani works in Buddhist studies. In 2015, she was attested as a part-time lecturer at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University.

Yukei Matsunaga worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Koyasan, Tohoku, and Kyushu universities. He held posts at Shuchiin University and Koyasan University, serving there as associate professor (~1964–1990) and director (1983).
Yuki Takatsukasa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Takatsukasa pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and was attested as a part-time lecturer there in 2017.

Yukihiko Asayama worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Asayama held posts as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as a Ministry of Education overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn, and held posts as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College.
Yukihisa Yamao specialized in history/archaeology and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1954–1963) and later held a post there from around 1975 to 2001.

Yukimasa Mizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku and Bukkyo universities. He served at Bukkyo University as associate professor (attested 1963) and president (~1979–1989), and headed Tokai Gakuen (~1992–2002) and Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen (~1999–2009).
Yukio Kotani works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Hanjiro Tominaga and was attested in 2001 as professor emeritus of comparative literature at Rissho University.
